# Skelpr

> Repository evidence with file:line citations, within a context budget.
> Connect a coding agent over MCP or use the standalone CLI with a configured
> generation provider. In MCP mode, the agent decides when to call Skelpr.

## Setup and data handling

- Python 3.10+ and Git. Standard setup verifies PostgreSQL and Qdrant, using
  Docker for local services. Plain `pip install skelpr` includes CLI and MCP.
- Running requires activation. Each activated machine uses one license seat.
  Managed leases check in automatically during licensed use at the interval set in the lease.
- In Skelpr 0.3.8, run `skelpr setup` in a terminal and choose Yes for MCP or No
  for the standalone CLI. Both modes verify embeddings. Standalone setup also
  verifies generation. MCP setup writes `.skelpr.yaml` and skips the Docker
  validation image by default. Direct options are `--embeddings-only` and
  `--configure`. After setup, run `skelpr index`. For MCP, also run
  `skelpr install-mcp`, reconnect the client, and call `skelpr_health`.
  No separate `init` step is needed after MCP setup.
- `skelpr setup --no-configure` sets up infrastructure only. `skelpr init`
  writes repository configuration without prompting. MCP and the HTTP API
  watch for changes by default.
- Hosted embeddings receive indexed text and queries. Hosted generation can
  receive prompts and selected source context. Remote storage and optional
  Langfuse tracing can receive source. The coding agent has its own data policy.
- Request an activation token by email. The website waitlist is for release updates.
- Context limits can exclude relevant evidence. Check reported gaps and request
  more context when needed. Empty search results do not prove absence.

## Workspaces and indexing

- Index one checkout or run setup, index and MCP installation once from a non-Git
  parent containing multiple Git checkouts. One root configuration and combined
  index cover the workspace; child configs are not merged. Source paths keep
  checkout prefixes. A Git parent uses normal checkout/submodule indexing.
- User-wide MCP registrations require `repository` to match the absolute indexed
  root. For a combined workspace, supply the parent path, not a child checkout.
- Each checkout supplies tracked files and non-ignored untracked files. Tracked
  files can remain eligible despite `.gitignore`. Loose parent files outside Git
  use Skelpr exclusions, not a parent `.gitignore`.
- Automatic exclusions always add logs, temporary files, backups, bytecode, Python
  tool caches and spreadsheet formats. Generated defaults also exclude dependency
  and build folders and recognized credential files. A custom YAML `ignore` list
  replaces the generated list; automatic exclusions still apply. Explicit `!`
  overrides can keep text fixtures but cannot restore Git-excluded untracked files.
- Recursive scanning has no configured depth limit and skips links/junctions.
  Binary, unreadable and oversized content is skipped; `indexing.max_file_bytes`
  defaults to 2,000,000 bytes. SQL, HTML, docs and patches can be indexed as text.
- MCP watching starts after the first licensed tool call. It catches up after
  restart and detects file changes, branch switches and child checkout membership
  changes. It embeds changed content only and retires removed or excluded entries.
  Defaults are 1-second polling plus a 1.5-second quiet period, then indexing time.
  Required services and the MCP process must stay running; failures retry with backoff.

## Case studies

- Sock Shop (September 2026): the historical report shows 59.3% fewer tokens and
  113 to 27 files opened. Retained artifacts do not fully reproduce the published aggregate.
- Django (November 2026), ten Codex tasks: total tokens 437,997 to 274,749 (37.27% fewer), native
  search/read calls 28 to 9, combined rubric score 89/96 to 91/96. Total wall time
  was 534.40 to 521.25 seconds; four tasks were slower with Skelpr.
- Django totals count all input, including cached input, plus output. These are retained
  matched comparisons across successive builds; the questions informed tuning.
  Q8 and Q10 used seeded defects. Neither study establishes general performance
  or results for one frozen release.
